scope: P4, P4X and the four P4Y pilots

mandatory_separation.evidence: 96 theorem-supported cells adjudicated against the unchanged 0.03 / |z|<=4 gate across P4 and P4X; 0 FAILED. The uniform and cauchy behaviours are the theorem's own proved failure modes F1 and F2 (THEOREM.md Sec. 9), i.e. confirmations.

findings.statement: The historical Route-A per-path summand A_m * S_tau^psi has an infinite second moment whenever the innovation law does, which for t1p5 (Student-t, nu=1.5) it does.
findings.mechanism: psi is bounded for t1p5 (sup|psi| = (nu+1)/(2 sqrt(nu)) = 1.0206) and tau has a geometric tail, so S_tau^psi has every moment. A_m does not: its alarm-causing increment Z_tau inherits the family's x^{-1.5} tail.
findings.documented_misstatement: estimators.py asserts that a heavy-tailed stopped gain 'has a finite variance but an infinite fourth moment'. False for t1p5. The batch-mean remedy it justifies does not repair an infinite second moment: block means of alpha-stable summands keep tail index alpha.

findings.statement: The historical Route-B CRN central difference is a rare-event estimator of a heavy-tailed jump.
findings.mechanism: Under CRN the pathwise difference of A_m is exactly -2h whenever the two shifted runs agree in stopping time and window indices, contributing exactly 1. All variance lives on the rare disagreement paths, where the value is O(Z_tau / 2h) with an amplification of 10 to 40.

findings.statement: The batch standard error reported for every heavy cell estimates a quantity that does not exist, so every derived z is unreliable.
findings.mechanism: Pilot-3 froze a normal-theory 1/sqrt(2(n-1)) uncertainty for a tail-index-1.5 law and was stopped. Pilot-4 showed that at b=250000 two independent 2048-block pools agreed to 2-4 % while one block carried 21-25 % of the squared deviation: agreement diagnostics cannot detect this, concentration diagnostics can.

findings.statement: Checkpoint A's precision precondition admits a state satisfying neither of its two branches, leaving 8 cells unadjudicable.
findings.mechanism: Section 8.1 permits at most one top-up; gate X6 requires each route to reach r* or be declared PRECISION_LIMITED from projected cost alone. A route that takes its top-up, misses r*, and hits no cap satisfies neither.
findings.note: A defect in the rule's totality, not a breach of it. P4X applied its own rule correctly and refused to count the cells as passes.

findings.statement: N_req targets an expectation where the gate needs a quantile, so the realised precision attains the target with probability near one half.
P4's Gaussian-consistency gate divided by one campaign's standard error alone, treating the closed Monte Carlo values as exact.
findings.status: ALREADY REPAIRED BY P4X obligation C5 as a new preregistered object. P4's own gate remains failed and untouched.

proved_failure_modes_confirmed_not_failu.resolution: THEOREM.md Sec. 9 F1: moving support breaks (A3) and the identity is FALSE with exact defect 2. Discharged analytically, by Route Q, and by an exact rational Arb certificate; 16/16 Monte Carlo cells corroborate at |z| 468-714.

THEOREM.md Sec. 9 F2: no first moment, so E|A_1| = infinity and the estimand does not exist. A two-route discrepancy statistic cannot express non-existence, which is why P4's counterexample gate could not fire. Discharged analytically by P4X obligation C4 with new compute NONE.

conclusion: F-01, F-02 and F-03 are one defect seen three times: the per-path summand carries the innovation law's tail. F-04 and F-05 are governance consequences of trying to buy precision the estimator cannot deliver. F-06 is independent and already repaired. A successor that changes only the allocation rule cannot work; P4X and P4Y demonstrated that across five campaigns.
